newsitem.title: USA: Computer Sciences wins Army contract.
newsitem.headline: Computer Sciences wins Army contract.

text.p: Computer Sciences Corp. said Wednesday it has won a U.S. Army contract worth an estimated $740 million to provide systems engineering and technical assistance at the U.S. Army Space and Strategic Defence Command in Alabama.
Mevatec, Nichols Research Corp. and Teledyne Brown Engineering were also awarded contracts, the company said.
The contract, which has no definite delivery dates, would be worth about $740 million if all options were exercised over a five-year period, Computer Sciences said.
Computer Sciences said it would support the Army's Space and Strategic Defence Command and the programme executive office for air and missile defence offices in Huntsville, Ala.
These offices manage the Army's research and development efforts in air and missile defence, the company said.

The company said it would also provide assistance to Space and Strategic Defence Command headquarters in Washington, the Army Space Command in Colorado and the High Energy Laser Systems test facility in New Mexico.
Computer Sciences said there were 10 subcontractors, including the Space and Science Technology Alliance, an Alabama university consortium.

Other teammates were ANRO Engineering, Camber Corp., EARTH TECH, EER Systems, JB Systems Engineering Support Co., Kaman Sciences Corp., Quality Research Inc., Systems Development Corp. and Tybrin Corp., the company said.
Falls Church, Va.-based Computer Sciences' stock rose $3.50 to $83.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.
